entry.content:
I've built websites on every major platform. Here's my honest ranking based on actually using them — not reading marketing pages. ## Quick Comparison | Rank | Tool | Best For | Free Tier | Starting Price | Rating | |------|------|----------|-----------|----------------|--------| | 1 | **Wix** | Beginners, small businesses | Yes | $17/mo | 4.5/5 | | 2 | **Squarespace** | Creative portfolios | No (14-day trial) | $16/mo | 4.4/5 | | 3 | **WordPress** | Blogs, complex sites | Yes (.com) | $4/mo (.com) | 4.3/5 | | 4 | **Webflow** | Designers, agencies | Yes | $14/mo | 4.2/5 | | 5 | **Shopify** | E-commerce | No (14-day trial) | $29/mo | 4.4/5 | | 6 | **Carrd** | One-page sites | Yes | $9/year | 4.0/5 | ## 1. Wix — Best Overall **Why it's #1:** Wix offers the best combination of ease of use, features, and value. The 800+ templates mean you'll find something that fits your industry, and the drag-and-drop editor is the most intuitive available. **Best for:** Small businesses, freelancers, restaurants, portfolios, blogs **Pros:** Free plan, 800+ templates, easiest editor, app market, built-in SEO tools **Cons:** Can't switch templates after publishing, free plan has branding, site speed can vary [Wix full review →](/nocode-launchpad/wix-review/) ## 2. Squarespace — Best for Design Squarespace templates are the most polished in the industry. If design quality matters more than template variety, Squarespace is the choice. **Best for:** Creative portfolios, photographers, designers, artists **Pros:** Beautiful templates, clean code, faster loading, better blogging **Cons:** No free plan, fewer templates, slightly harder to learn [Wix vs Squarespace comparison →](/nocode-launchpad/wix-vs-squarespace/) ## 3. WordPress — Most Flexible WordPress powers 40%+ of the web. It's the most flexible option but requires more technical knowledge — you'll manage hosting, updates, and security yourself. **Best for:** Blogs, complex sites, advanced SEO, custom functionality **Pros:** Unlimited flexibility, 50,000+ plugins, best SEO, largest community **Cons:** Steep learning curve, requires maintenance, hosting costs extra ## 4. Webflow — Best for Designers Webflow gives designers pixel-perfect control without writing code. It's more powerful than Wix but harder to learn. **Best for:** Designers, agencies, marketing sites, portfolios **Pros:** Pixel-perfect control, clean code export, built-in CMS, animations **Cons:** Steeper learning curve, no free plan on custom domains, more expensive ## 5. Shopify — Best for E-commerce If you're building an online store, Shopify is the specialist. It handles products, payments, shipping, and inventory better than any general-purpose builder. **Best for:** Online stores, dropshipping, e-commerce businesses **Pros:** Best e-commerce features, 6,000+ apps, payment processing, shipping **Cons:** More expensive ($29/mo+), transaction fees on non-Shopify payments, not for non-store sites ## 6. Carrd — Best for Simple Sites Carrd builds beautiful one-page sites for $9/year. If you just need a landing page, link-in-bio, or simple portfolio, Carrd is the cheapest option. **Best for:** Landing pages, link-in-bio sites, simple portfolios **Pros:** Incredibly cheap ($9/year), beautiful templates, fast setup **Cons:** One-page only, no blogging, limited functionality ## How to Choose | Your Situation | Best Choice | |---------------|-------------| | First website, want it easy | Wix | | Creative portfolio | Squarespace | | Blog with lots of content | WordPress | | Need design control | Webflow | | Online store | Shopify | | Simple landing page | Carrd | For most people, **start with Wix**. The free plan lets you test, and upgrading is straightforward when you're ready.

Our Top Pick: Wix

The easiest way to build a professional website. Start free.

Try Wix Free
## FAQ ### What is the best website builder in 2026? Wix is our top pick for most users. It offers 800+ templates, a free plan, and the easiest drag-and-drop editor. For creative portfolios, Squarespace has more polished designs. For maximum flexibility, WordPress. ### Can I build a website for free? Yes, Wix and WordPress.com both have free plans. Free plans include platform branding and subdomains. Paid plans ($12-30/month) remove branding and add custom domains. ### Which website builder is best for SEO? WordPress is the best for SEO with plugins like Yoast and Rank Math. Wix and Squarespace have good built-in SEO tools. For most small businesses, any of these platforms handle SEO adequately. ### Should I use WordPress or a website builder? Use a website builder (Wix, Squarespace) if you want simplicity and don't want to manage hosting, updates, or security. Use WordPress if you need maximum flexibility, advanced SEO, or complex functionality. ### How much does a website cost in 2026? With a website builder: $0-30/month for most sites. With WordPress: $5-30/month for hosting plus domain ($12/year). Custom development: $3,000-$50,000+. Website builders are the cheapest option for simple sites. ## Related Articles - [Wix Review 2026: Features, Pricing, and Is It Worth It?](/nocode-launchpad/wix-review/) - [Wix vs Squarespace 2026: Which Should You Choose?](/nocode-launchpad/wix-vs-squarespace/) - [Best No-Code App Builders in 2026](/nocode-launchpad/best-no-code-app-builders/)

entry.title: Wix vs Squarespace 2026: Which Website Builder Should You Choose?

link.title: Wix vs Squarespace 2026: Which Website Builder Should You Choose?

entry.content:
Wix and Squarespace are the two biggest website builders. I've used both for client projects — here's how they actually compare. ## Quick Verdict | | Wix | Squarespace | |---|-----|-------------| | **Best for** | Beginners, small businesses | Creative portfolios, aesthetics | | **Ease of use** | Easier | Slightly harder | | **Templates** | 800+ | 100+ (more polished) | | **Free plan** | Yes | No (14-day trial) | | **Starting price** | $17/mo | $16/mo | | **Our rating** | 4.5/5 | 4.4/5 | **Choose Wix** for flexibility and ease of use. **Choose Squarespace** for design quality and creative portfolios. ## Feature Comparison | Feature | Wix | Squarespace | |---------|-----|-------------| | Drag-and-drop editor | Yes (free-form) | Yes (structured) | | Templates | 800+ | 100+ | | Free plan | Yes | No | | Custom domain | Paid plans | Paid plans | | E-commerce | Business plans | Business plans | | Blogging | Basic | Better | | SEO tools | Good | Good | | App market | Yes (250+) | Limited extensions | | Mobile editing | Yes | Yes | | Code injection | Yes | Yes | | Member areas | Yes | Yes | ## Ease of Use ### Wix Wix's editor is free-form — you can drag elements anywhere on the page. This gives you freedom but can lead to inconsistent layouts if you're not careful. The ADI (Artificial Design Intelligence) feature can auto-generate a site based on your answers. It's a good starting point for absolute beginners. ### Squarespace Squarespace uses a structured editor — elements snap to a grid. This keeps your design clean and consistent but gives you less freedom. The editor is slightly harder to learn but produces more professional results by default. ## Templates ### Wix: 800+ Templates Wix has one of the largest template libraries. Templates are organized by industry — restaurants, portfolios, stores, services, and more. **Downside:** Once you choose a template and publish, you can't switch. Choose carefully. ### Squarespace: 100+ Templates Squarespace has fewer templates but they're more polished. Every template looks professional out of the box. **Upside:** You can switch templates after publishing (on the old version — check current policy). ## E-commerce Both platforms offer e-commerce on business plans: | | Wix | Squarespace | |---|-----|-------------| | **Starting plan** | Business ($36/mo) | Business ($33/mo) | | **Transaction fee** | 0% | 3% on Business plan | | **Payment gateways** | Multiple | Stripe, PayPal | | **Abandoned cart** | Yes | Yes (higher plans) | | **Inventory management** | Yes | Yes | | **Shipping labels** | Yes | Yes | For serious e-commerce, both work. Squarespace has cleaner product pages; Wix has more e-commerce features. ## Blogging Squarespace wins for blogging. Its blog layouts are more refined, the editor is better for long-form content, and the category/tag system is more flexible. Wix blogging is functional but basic. If blogging is central to your site, Squarespace is the better choice. ## SEO Both platforms have improved their SEO tools significantly: | | Wix | Squarespace | |---|-----|-------------| | **Meta tags** | Customizable | Customizable | | **URL structure** | Clean | Clean | | **Sitemap** | Auto-generated | Auto-generated | | **301 redirects** | Yes | Yes | | **Structured data** | Yes | Yes | | **Page speed** | Can be slow | Generally faster | For most small business SEO needs, both are adequate. Squarespace tends to produce faster-loading sites. ## Pricing | | Wix | Squarespace | |---|-----|-------------| | **Free plan** | Yes | No | | **Personal** | $17/mo | $16/mo | | **Business** | $29/mo | $23/mo | | **E-commerce** | $36/mo | $33/mo | | **Advanced** | $159/mo | $65/mo | Prices are similar. Wix's free plan is a significant advantage if you want to test before committing. ## When to Choose Wix - You want a free plan to test - You need maximum template variety - You're a beginner who wants simplicity - You need an app market for extra features - You want drag-and-drop freedom ## When to Choose Squarespace - Design quality is your top priority - You're building a creative portfolio - Blogging is central to your site - You want cleaner, faster-loading pages - You prefer structured, consistent layouts

Try Wix Free

Start building your website with Wix's free plan. No credit card required.

Try Wix Free
## FAQ ### Is Wix better than Squarespace? Wix is easier to use and has more templates. Squarespace has more polished designs and better for creative portfolios. Neither is objectively better — it depends on your priorities. ### Which is cheaper, Wix or Squarespace? Wix has a free plan (Squarespace doesn't). Paid plans are similar: Wix starts at $17/mo, Squarespace at $16/mo. For e-commerce, both charge around $27-33/mo. ### Can I switch from Wix to Squarespace? There's no direct migration. You'd rebuild your site on the new platform. Content can be exported/imported in some cases, but design and structure need to be recreated. ### Which has better templates, Wix or Squarespace? Wix has more templates (800+ vs 100+). Squarespace templates are more polished and cohesive. If you want quantity and variety, choose Wix. If you want refined design quality, choose Squarespace. ### Is Squarespace better for portfolios? Yes, Squarespace is generally better for creative portfolios. Its templates are designed with photographers, designers, and artists in mind. The layouts are more gallery-focused and visually refined. ## Related Articles - [Wix Review 2026: Features, Pricing, and Is It Worth It?](/nocode-launchpad/wix-review/) - [Best Website Builders in 2026](/nocode-launchpad/best-website-builders/) - [Base44 Review 2026: Best No-Code App Builder?](/nocode-launchpad/base44-review/)

entry.title: I Built an AI Tutor App with Base44 — And It Uses the Socratic Method

link.title: I Built an AI Tutor App with Base44 — And It Uses the Socratic Method

entry.content:
## Why Build an AI Tutor?
Most tutoring apps just give you the answer. That's not how learning works. The **Socratic method** — asking guiding questions instead of providing answers — has been proven to help students understand concepts deeper and retain information longer.
I wanted to build an app that uses this approach, powered by AI. And I wanted to build it without writing a single line of code.
## What I Built
**Thinkerwell** — a personalized AI tutoring app that:
- Uses the **Socratic method** to guide students to answers through questions - Adapts to each student's **grade level** and **preferred learning style** - Tracks **streaks, progress, and mastery** across subjects - Supports multiple subjects: math, science, history, programming, and more - Includes a **courses dashboard** where students can browse and track their learning path
![Thinkerwell — Home Page with Owl Mascot](/assets/images/app-screenshots/tutor-app-home.webp)
### The Owl Mascot
The app features a friendly **robot owl mascot** — a wise tutor character that guides students through their learning journey. The owl appears on the home page, onboarding flow, and quiz sessions, giving the app a warm, approachable feel.
### How the Socratic Method Works in the App
Instead of saying "The answer is 42," the tutor asks:
1. **"What do you already know about this problem?"** — Gets the student thinking 2. **"What would happen if we tried X?"** — Guides exploration 3. **"Can you see a pattern here?"** — Helps discover the solution 4. **"Why do you think that works?"** — Reinforces understanding
The student arrives at the answer themselves — which means they actually understand it.
![Thinkerwell — Onboarding Flow](/assets/images/app-screenshots/tutor-app-onboarding.webp)
